overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating outside a posted meeting before its September 12 session; the July polling claim was untimely and the procedural and ethics claims were outside the law.

allegations.summary: Members allegedly discussed a subdivision plan by private conversation before the September 12 meeting began, outside any posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: Private deliberations such as these feed the secrecy the Open Meeting Law was enacted to eliminate.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly polled board members by email about a subdivision plan in July; the AG found this claim untimely, though it reminded the Board that polling is prohibited.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, that portion of the complaint is untimely and we decline to review it.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to close a public hearing before voting at the September 12 meeting; the AG said procedural claims fall outside the law.
allegations.key_passage: allegations of a conflict of interest, of ethical violations and of improper voting procedure during a meeting, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a conflict of interest and ethics violations by the board chair; these are outside the Open Meeting Law and were declined.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review the allegations of procedural irregularity, ethics violations or conflict of interest, as those claims fall outside of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law’s requirements and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
